name: lite3-pro-parametric-model
title: Lite3 LiDAR high-fidelity printable replica
description: Current target is Dr Sun's purchased current Lite3 Pro hardware revision with the long white, two-front-recess compute enclosure. Ten physical measurement photos define a 65 mm front pair and uncertainty-bearing scaffold. A user-provided textured GLB scan is archived, isolated from its room scene, metre-scale checked, corrected to a right-handed +X-front/+Y-left/+Z-up reference, and used to recover the notched enclosure footprint. Legacy Pro V1.0.7, Venture/J17A hardware, and the local Exploration/Experience B-rep remain separate evidence tracks. A compact source-geometry sensor layout fits the measured front zone, but the printable lower adapter remains blocked on receiver thread/depth, centre-axis load path, cable/service sweeps, and human placement review.
creator: sun
notes: Historical Rev A/Rev B and V1 artifacts remain negative or upper-module evidence only. On 2026-07-29 Dr Sun confirmed the purchased unit is a newer current Lite3 Pro revision. The legacy 2024 Pro manual publishes 4 x M3 on 74 x 94 mm, 445 mm height, and 12.7 kg; the official 2025 brochure reports current Pro at 450 mm and 12.9 kg but publishes no hole drawing. The official FAST-LIVO2 repository at commit 624b45c explicitly scopes its printable hardware to Venture only. On 2026-07-30 ten physical photos were archived and validated. They support a 65.0 +/- 1.0 mm front-axis pitch, a centre visible candidate about 75 mm rearward, a compute front about 100 mm rearward, and an approximately 200 x 100 x 50 mm enclosure. The user-provided GLB physical scan is also archived with hash 294bf7e1..., parses as 353508 vertices and 617023 triangles, and includes floor/room geometry. An enclosure-top fit corrects yaw by -160.777014948 deg and yields an approximately 199.585 x 108.618 mm span; corrected photos disambiguate the rounded nose as +X/front. A 10025-sample footprint analysis recovers two approximately 30 mm front-side recesses with nominal inner edges at Y=-42/+44 mm; the nominal B-rep now uses the notched polygon while the collision keep-out remains rectangular. Derived OBJ/STL/PLY outputs are reference-only and not manufacturing geometry. A cleanly reimported current-Pro proxy and expanded keep-out exist with no printable STL. The retained approximately 153.7 mm carrier exceeds the measured front zone by approximately 37.7 mm. A compact 110 x 115 mm zero-thickness layout uses the official Mid-360 B-rep, related-source S410 B-rep, and official D435i envelope; it has zero sensor/expanded-box intersection, 6.0 mm S410 clearance, and 2.5 mm D435i-to-nose clearance. A separate scan-registered Rev B upper review preserves source J20A/MID-360/S410 transforms and stays 5.0 mm ahead of the conservative keep-out. Its separate D435i support study is one solid with the official 45 mm camera pitch and zero modeled penetration, but the current camera envelope overhangs the measured nose by approximately 24.198 mm and is not placement-accepted. The lower-adapter gate now consumes the Rev B two-recess footprint and Y=[-57,+60] mm keep-out; an A/B/C/D visual card and machine-readable request define the remaining thread, usable-depth, recess, material, insert, load-path, and service-clearance evidence. The receiver accepted count remains zero. No current-Pro lower adapter solid, screw selection, print release, or physical-fit claim exists.
